Outcome_variable.evidence_source: [024_general_discussion] The aim of this study was to examine how implicit theories of intelligence are associated with subjective well-being. Results of the two studies showed that entity theory of intelligence was detrimental to certain aspects of well-being. Entity theory positively predicted negative affect both concurrently (Study 1) and prospectively (Study 2). The relationship between entity theory and life satisfaction was less robust. In Study 2, T1 entity theory did not predict T2 life satisfaction. Entity theory likewise did not predict positive affect across both studies. | Figure 1.
